title: aditi-mehra-inference-cliffnotes-rapid-fire-reads
content:
Quick cliffnotes + action items from a bunch of papers/blogs I skimmed during the transit week. Mostly for myself: light summaries, why it might matter for serving runtime, cheap experiments to try, and quick hypotheses. Chaotic — forgive the jumps.

1) "Adaptive Prefix Eviction for Long-context LMs" (paper, arXiv 2609.01234) — quick take
- Idea: dynamic eviction of cached KV prefixes based on uncertainty estimates + downstream token-utility score. Instead of LRU/Timestamp, compute a per-prefix retention score = importance_estimate * recency_decay. Importance_estimate derived from attention overlap + predicted next-token surprisal when prefix is present.
- Why interesting for Redwood: could reduce memory pressure on long-session customers while preserving high-value context. Less blunt than fixed TTLs or length caps.
- Implementation sketch for prototype: instrument current KV-cache to log attention overlap stats per prefix (cheap approx via top-k attention mass). Add a small periodic scorer process that tags prefixes for eviction.
- Risks/unknowns: cost of computing importance_estimate at high QPS; stability of scorer leading to oscillation (evict then re-fetch).
- Cheap experiment: run offline trace replay on two weeks of conversation logs (anonymized) -> simulate adaptive eviction vs LRU and measure token re-generation rate, average latency bump, and cache hit ratio.
- Metric to track: re-generation qps per 1k requests, 95th latency when cache-miss on hot prefix, % of tokens saved.

2) "Kernel-aware Scheduling for Heterogeneous GPUs" (conference talk notes) — quick take
- People are scheduling kernel shapes (matmul dims, head counts, kv-cache ops) to map onto A100 vs H100 vs L4d. Idea: maintain small profile per model-variant (seq-len distribution, kernel shapes) and use a scoring function in the scheduler to prefer device with best predicted p99 latency given current batch mix.
- For Redwood Dedicated: this could power cost-aware routing (if H100 is busy, route to cheaper dev that still meets SLO with slightly different quantized model).
- Experiment idea: take a 3-model workload (base/quant4/int8) and run an emulated scheduler that admits tasks until predicted p99 exceeds threshold; compare throughput and cost vs current naive round-robin.
- Notes to self: need per-variant microbenchmarks (seq len 32/128/512/2048) and a compact predictor (linear model maybe) rather than heavy ML model.

3) "Prefetching KV shards using request graph priors" (blog + repo) — quick take
- Premise: requests during a session have a graph structure (turns, references). Use light-weight predictor (n-gram-ish over token clusters or embedding-similarity) to decide which remote KV shards to prefetch when a request lands.
- Playground idea: adapt existing async prefetcher in runtime to accept a "prefetch hint" that indicates likely top-3 shard ids. Measure latency delta for 1% of sessions instrumented.
- Danger: wasted prefetching increases egress / memory churn. Need strict budget: only prefetch when estimated hit_prob > 0.6 and expected latency saving > cost.

4) Short paper: "Quantization drop-in probes" (two-page) — takeaways
- Simple eval harness that runs a small balanced prompt set to detect quality regressions when switching quantization or per-layer fallback. Shows early-warning signals for hallucination increases and token-level perplexity drift.
- Action: propose adding a 30-prompt smoke-test to CI for model rollouts (hosted-api). If any hallucination metric jumps > 5% raise a canary alert.

Notes to self / random heuristics observed in these reads:
- Attention-overlap as a cheap importance proxy seems recurrent — approximate with top-k token overlap heuristics from the last N tokens.
- Eviction oscillation likely needs hysteresis: once evicted, tag prefix "cooldown" for X minutes before re-populate without explicit user signal.
- Much of the scheduler work is only worth it if you have mixed hardware footprints and tight slot cost differences (Dedicated customers with mixed fleets).

Small experiment plan (week-by-week quick sprints)
- Week 1: export 7 days of anonymized session traces and write a simulator that can replay with different eviction policies (LRU, TTL-60m, adaptive-score). This is low-cost CPU job and should give hit-rate vs regens.
- Week 2: build a minimal scorer for prefixes (approx top-k attention mass + age decay) and run in simulation; collect metrics.
- Week 3: wire a non-blocking prefetch hint into dev runtime (flagged) and run canary on 1% of sessions for 48h. Measure wasted prefetch % and latency P50/P95 improvement.
- Week 4: implement small CI quantization smoke test for the hosted model catalog and run on the next model push.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to safely anonymize the traces such that we keep attention/clique signals but strip PII? Talk to privacy team. (TODO: ping Priya R. about trace scrubber template)
- What storage accounting changes if we adopt short-lived prefetch caches? Need input from infra-cost team; file follow-up JIRA.
- Where to expose policy knobs in Console? Manual toggle for adaptive-eviction per-customer vs global default.

Links I want to re-read quickly:
- adaptive prefix eviction (arXiv:2609.01234) 
- kernel-aware scheduling slides (internal recording link in slack thread) 
- kv prefetch repo (github link in linked_artifacts)

Random scattered thoughts (notes-to-self):
- This family of ideas tends to trade off small increases in compute for bigger decreases in memory and egress — which is a good leverage point for Dedicated customers with expensive SRAM/GPU memory constraints.
- Keep the first prototypes purely simulation-based; avoid changing production runtime until we see clear win on replayed logs.
- Consider a "prefix tiering" concept: hot prefixes pinned in fast memory, warm prefixes in compressed quantized storage (allow partial restore), cold prefixes evicted. Might combine well with quant-aware compression.

Immediate next actions (today)
- Create JIRA ticket skeleton: ENG-XXXX adaptive-eviction-sim + attach sample trace schema.
- DM Priya R. for trace scrubber template.
- Add a 30-prompt quantization smoke test draft to the model-rollout checklist in Confluence.

-- end of cliffnotes --

Notes are messy. Will iterate when I turn sim results into numbers. If Lena or Evan have time, want a 30-minute sync to prioritize which experiment to run first (sim vs prefetch prototype).
